Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Asset Management Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Asset Management's Third Quarter 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Distribution; Robert Kline, Head of Operations; and Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by impressive organic growth rates and expanding market share across key segments. Our assets under management grew to $1.82 trillion, reflecting the strength of our franchise even in a resilient yet volatile market environment.

From a high level, our organic AUM growth rate hit 9.2% year-over-year for the quarter, accelerating from 7.8% in the prior year period and surpassing the industry average of 6.1% according to Morningstar Direct data. Over the trailing 12 months, this figure stands at 11.5%, powered by quarterly net new money inflows of $28.4 billion—our strongest since late 2021. This momentum persisted despite a 2.3% dip in the S&P 500 and ongoing fixed income challenges from higher yields.

Breaking it down by asset class, equities led with 12.1% organic growth, fueled by $14.2 billion in inflows to active and smart-beta offerings where our large-cap growth strategies outperformed benchmarks by 210 basis points on a beta-adjusted basis, securing top-quartile Lipper rankings in most funds. ESG equity sleeves alone drew $4.1 billion, tapping into regulatory tailwinds like EU SFDR updates. Fixed income saw 7.8% growth with $7.9 billion inflows, as our core-plus approaches returned 3.4% gross against the Bloomberg Aggregate's meager 1.2%, helping us capture share from peers experiencing outflows. Alternatives and multi-asset shone brightest at 15.3% growth and $6.3 billion inflows, highlighted by our new private credit opportunities fund scaling to $1.2 billion. Even passive ETFs and index products expanded 10.7% organically with $5 billion inflows, thanks to competitive 12 basis point fees on core equity trackers.

Regionally, North America at 72% of AUM delivered 10.4% growth with $18 billion year-to-date institutional wins, including a major public pension carve-out. EMEA accelerated to 8.9% with €4.5 billion flows post-UCITS enhancements, gaining on competitors like Amundi. APAC hit 11.2% via sovereign wealth fund mandates in sustainable strategies. On market share, we've gained 45 basis points year-to-date in U.S. equities to 1.8% per eVestment, 62 basis points in global alternatives to 2.4%, and lifted ETF smart-beta share to 3.1% per ETFGI.

This outperformance stems from our tech-enabled distribution via the PinnacleFlow platform, cutting onboarding by 60%; persistent alpha with 78% of strategies beating three-year benchmarks; and key hires plus partnerships accelerating privates growth. We expect 9-11% organic growth for full-year 2024 with $105-115 billion in net new money, positioning us to compound share through cycles.

I'll now turn it over to Michael for the financial details.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Asset Management delivered strong results in the third quarter. Our revenue was $850 million, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust management fee revenue and stable average fee rates amid industry pressures.

Thank you for that context, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Let me dive deeper into our management fee revenue and average fee rate trends for Q3 fiscal 2024, ended September 30th. These fees form the core of our recurring revenue, calculated as a percentage of average AUM, net of performance fee offsets. They fund our research platforms and distribution expansion.

Headline figures: Q3 management fee revenue reached $452 million, up 9% year-over-year from $415 million and 3% sequentially from $439 million in Q2. This beat the industry's 5-6% average per Morningstar, thanks to organic AUM growth and fee discipline despite compression headwinds.

Ending AUM was $1.82 trillion, up 8% YoY from prior levels, with $12 billion quarterly net inflows—strongest since late 2022. Average AUM for the quarter was around $1.75 trillion, up 7% YoY. Market appreciation added 4 points, with equities outperforming by 120 basis points gross amid S&P gains; inflows contributed 5 points, offset by minor FX drag from 25% international mix.

Blended average fee rate held at 45.2 basis points, down just 1.5 bps YoY from 46.7 bps and flat sequentially. This resilience reflects our shift from commoditized beta, as industry rates fell to 42 bps from 48 bps five years ago per McKinsey, driven by ETF growth like BlackRock's $3 trillion iShares at sub-10 bps.

By asset class: Equities (52% AUM) at 52 bps, down 3 bps on $4 billion legacy outflows but offset by $8 billion into smart-beta ETFs like our Equity Momentum ETF at 28 bps premium to Vanguard. Fixed income (22%) at 38 bps, up 1 bp on $6 billion inflows to short-duration ESG munis outperforming by 75 bps. Alternatives (18%) excelled at 92 bps, up 4 bps with $5 billion into private credit yielding 11% net. Multi-asset/cash (8%) dipped to 32 bps on money market shifts but added $3 billion.

Regionally, North America (68% fees) up 11% on 401(k)/RIA growth with Unified Managed Accounts at $45 billion; EMEA (20%) flat at €85 billion as MiFID pressures eased; APAC (12%) up 15% to A$120 billion via UCITS ETFs and local tie-ups.

Strategically, pillars include product innovation like four active ETFs including Climate Alpha at 45 bps with $2 billion AUM; SMAs at $120 billion for 55-65 bps via tax-alpha; and alternatives ramp to 25% mix by 2026 for 200 bps accretion. Q4 fees guided at $460-470 million at 45 bps, with 15% margins for M&A like our recent credit boutique buy.

Before moving on, a quick note on our capital allocation strategy, a key driver of shareholder value with $1.82 trillion AUM up 14% YoY on $45 billion inflows. Our framework balances shareholder returns, growth investments, and M&A with $4.2 billion dry powder and 45% margins.

First, shareholder returns: $1.1 billion YTD (85% free cash flow), with dividend up 8% to $0.42/share yielding 2.8%, and $650 million buybacks retiring 2.1% float at $285—15% below book value—with $850 million left targeting 3-5% dilution offset for 7% EPS growth.

Second, growth reinvestments: $450 million annually (15-20% free cash), including $60 million to ApexOne robo-advisory at $180 billion AUM with 28% client growth; $40 million scaling $250 billion alts like $5 billion private credit at 9-11% IRRs; $20 million to Quantum Alpha engine boosting Sharpe to 1.25.

Third, M&A: $750 million Horizon ESG buy adding 25 bps margins; pipeline at 10x EV/EBITDA for privates/RIAs.

Balance sheet is fortress-like: 0.8x net debt/EBITDA, 250% liquidity, stress-tested. 2025 free cash $3.2 billion allocated 75% shareholders, 15% capex, 10% M&A for 12-15% book value CAGR. Hybrid model, geo tilts, AI unlock $50 billion AUM potential for 18% TSR.

This positions us strongly. Over to David.

David Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging innovative product launches and maintaining superior fund performance rankings. We launched several new products this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with significant inflows and top ratings.

Thank you, Sarah—or Michael—and good morning. Let me detail our new product launches and fund performance rankings, highlighting Pinnacle's innovation and alpha generation amid inflation, geopolitics, and Fed cuts.

New launches: Three flagships raised $4.2 billion in first 45 days, YTD $7.8 billion up 35%. Pinnacle AI Innovators ETF (PAII) at 0.45% ER targets AI infrastructure (NVIDIA, TSMC, Palantir) with quant models on satellite/patent data; up 22% YTD beating index by 8 points, $1.9 billion AUM from RIAs. Pinnacle Global ESG Credit Fund at 0.65% ER for IG/HY corporates with MSCI screens; 4.2% yield, $1.5 billion AUM mostly EMEA (55%) under SFDR. Pinnacle Alternatives Multi-Strategy UCITS at 8-10% vol combines privates; $900 million from Middle East SWFs.

Backed by $150 million in Pinnacle AlphaForge using reinforcement learning for 15% lower tracking error, 90-day launches.

Performance: 82% AUM top-two Morningstar quartiles (3yr), 64% equity/71% FI 4/5-star vs. 48% peer median. Standouts: Large Cap Growth (PLCGX) Gold Medalist, top 1% 5yr at 15.2% net (+210 bps S&P); Emerging Markets 5-star, 12.8% 1yr (+350 bps MSCI EM) via India/Mexico. Lipper: 77% top-two 3yr, incl. short-duration topper at 4.1%.

Regional: U.S. equities 85% top-quartile; EMEA FI 79%; APAC EM debt +150 bps. Hybrid model: active alpha 120 bps, passive 0.03% fees; 96% retention via STAR framework.

Ahead: Defense ETF, small-cap value; $25-30 billion inflows, top-decile via quant edge.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our equity and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in North America and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by positive total net flows and breakdowns by channel.

Thank you, David. For Q3 ended September 30th, total net inflows were $28.4 billion, YTD $92.7 billion, 6.2% organic growth TTM $115.2 billion—strongest since 2021 amid rates/geopolitics.

By product: ETFs/index $16.8 billion (up 24% QoQ) led by Core Equity $9.2 billion on AI rally, new Climate/AI ETFs $2.1 billion; active equities/multi $8.5 billion on small/mid outperformance +320 bps; alts $7.2 billion (up 35% YoY) private credit $12.4 billion commitments; FI/cash -$4.1 billion offset by bonds.

By channel: Institutional $19.6 billion (69%) with $3.5 billion pension infrastructure win; retail/wealth $8.8 billion via Schwab/Fidelity, target-date $4.2 billion.

Regional: Americas $23.3 billion (82%), EMEA $3.4 billion UCITS/ESG, APAC $1.7 billion (42% YoY) China/Singapore.

By channel detail: Institutional $11.4 billion (63%) record, 4.1% margin; U.S. pension $3.2 billion, EMEA SWF $2.1 billion ESG. Retail $4.7 billion (26%), 2.8% margin; ETFs $2.4 billion, robo 45k accounts. Alts $2.1 billion (11%), private credit $1.3 billion, PE $500 million; regional split NA/EMEA/APAC.

PinnacleFlow AI boosts retention 18%, blockchain NAVs. Q4 guide $25-30 billion, pipeline $40 billion.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on advancing our digital platform investments.

Thank you, Lisa, and good morning. Our tech and digital investments—$285 million past 12 months up 22%, 4.5% opex—are our moat against fee pressure and fintechs.

Platform modernization: Phase 2 cloud migration (AWS/GCP) cut trade speeds 28% to <50ms, STP fails 35% for $1.2T AUM, Aladdin-par. RegTech automates 92% MiFID/SFDR reporting, saved $12M fines; APAC AUM +18% to $320B via HKEX APIs.

AI/data: AlphaForge ML on 15yr data +150 bps outperformance, NLP ESG scores for 68% client demand; personalization 87% accuracy, $45B YTD digital inflows +52%.

Client platforms: WealthHub app 2.8M users, DAU +41%, NPS 74; fractional ETFs, stress-tests. Blockchain tokenized $500M illiquids -200 bps premium.

Regional: NA millennial 30% retail; EMEA GDPR advice +14%; APAC Tencent/Ant 1.2M users 40% CAGR; LatAm voice trading.

FY24 $320M budget, 40% genAI; cyber $40M SOC2; 250 engineers 15% headcount. 3.2x ROI supports 8% AUM/12-15% EPS growth.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and liquidity risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes proactive measures embedded in our capital allocation, such as maintaining AAA-rated balance sheet with 0.8x net debt, 250% liquidity, laddered corporates, and stress tests for rate shocks/drawdowns. Our approach de-risks against higher-for-longer rates, fee caps, outflows, ensuring flexibility for strategic priorities.

Sarah Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes sustaining organic momentum, fee resilience via alts/product innovation, tech-driven distribution, and disciplined allocation returning 18% TSR YTD.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Morningstar.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on management fee revenue trends and fee rate pressures?

Sarah Thompson: Good question, John. As Michael detailed, Q3 fees hit $452 million up 9% YoY, outpacing industry on AUM growth and mix shift. Blended rate stable at 45.2 bps via smart-beta at 28 bps, alts 92 bps, SMAs 55-65 bps. Proactive on innovation, personalization, alts ramp to counter ETF compression—Q4 guide solid.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on total net flows breakdown?

Michael Chen: Absolutely. $28.4 billion quarterly, strong across ETFs $16.8B, alts $7.2B, institutional dominant at $19.6B. Tech like PinnacleFlow aiding retention/conversion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Bloomberg.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Pinnacle Large Cap Growth Fund?

David Patel: Sure, Emily. PLCGX earned Morningstar Gold, top 1% 5-year at 15.2% net +210 bps S&P, from mega-tech overweight, tactical cyclicals trim. 82% AUM top-quartiles overall.

Emily Chen: And how is the new product PAII performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Wong: Exceeding targets—$1.9B AUM, 22% YTD +8pp vs. AI index, strong RIA uptake on quant edge for semis/cloud.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs.

David Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Robert Kline: Happy to, David. Cloud migration slashed STP fails 35%, trades <50ms; AI personalization +$45B flows; WealthHub NPS 74, blockchain tokenization unlocks liquidity. 3.2x ROI driving margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with JPMorgan.

Maria Gonzalez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Great point, Maria. Regs like SFDR/MiFID navigated via 92% automated reporting, no fines. Balance sheet fortress: 0.8x leverage, stress-tested; monitoring vol/liquidity tightly, de-risked portfolio tilts preserve optionality amid Fed/ECB paths.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Pinnacle Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
